root_cause_label: Wrong I/O Interpretation (Treats Input as Single Triplet Instead of 20 Indexed Triplets) + Off-by-One Output Naming (Writes solution_1..solution_20 Instead of solution_0..solution_19)
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent violates the task's explicit multi-instance I/O specification by processing the inputs as a single heuristically selected triplet instead of 20 indexed triplets, and further fails by writing misnumbered output files (solution_1 through solution_20) instead of the required solution_0 through solution_19.
t_err_evidence: In step 3 the agent writes reconstruct.py with find_input_files() that heuristically picks one row/col/val file (the first matching each keyword) rather than iterating over row_idx_{i}.txt/col_idx_{i}.txt/observed_vals_{i}.txt for i in 0..19, and the output loop is range(1,21) writing solution_1..solution_20 instead of solution_0..solution_19.
t_commit_evidence: In step 4 the agent runs python3 reconstruct.py, executing the flawed script and physically creating the wrong output files (solution_1..solution_20), after which the incorrect state is locked in.
t_surface_evidence: In step 5 ls -la /app/solution_*.txt shows solution_1.txt through solution_20.txt with no solution_0.txt present, visibly demonstrating the off-by-one naming error; the agent does not acknowledge this discrepancy.
trigger_explanation: Despite observing 20 indexed triplets in steps 1-2 (row_idx_0..19, col_idx_0..19, observed_vals_0..19), the agent wrote a script that ignores the indexed structure entirely, using heuristic filename matching to pick one triplet and independently generating 20 outputs from it. The agent also failed to match the 0-indexed output naming requirement (solution_0..solution_19), using 1-indexed (solution_1..solution_20) instead. Both errors reflect dropping or never internalizing the explicit multi-instance I/O contract implicit in the file naming convention.
